note.text:
Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. It exists in three states:
• Solid (stone, ice, wood): fixed shape and fixed volume. Particles are very close, in fixed places; they only vibrate.
• Liquid (water, palm oil, kerosene): no fixed shape, it takes the shape of its container; fixed volume; it flows. Particles are close but can move past each other.
• Gas (air, steam, oxygen): no fixed shape and no fixed volume; it spreads to fill its container and can be squashed. Particles are far apart and move fast.
The same substance can be in all three states: ice, water and steam.

worked_example.problem: Why can we pump more air into a football, but not more water into a full bottle?
steps: Air is a gas: its particles are far apart, so they can be pushed closer together (compressed).
Water is a liquid: its particles are already close together, so it cannot be squashed.
worked_example.answer: Gas particles are far apart and can be squashed together; liquid particles are already close.

cards.idea: Matter has three states: solid, liquid and gas.
example: Solid: a stone. Liquid: palm oil. Gas: the air in a football.

cards.idea: A solid keeps its shape. A liquid takes the shape of its container but keeps its volume. A gas fills its container.
example: Pour water from a bottle into a bowl: the shape changes, the volume stays the same.

cards.idea: Particles: very close and fixed in a solid; close but moving in a liquid; far apart and fast in a gas.
example: That is why a gas can be squashed, but a liquid cannot.
